title: The global principle of word forms
summary: Only verbs, adjectives and the copula change, they change only their last kana, and they always do it by the same stem-and-helper system.

blocks.text: Until now you met the stem system one piece at a time. This lesson puts the whole picture in one place. Japanese has two kinds of words: **static words**, which never change (nearly all nouns), and **active words**, which can be an engine: verbs, adjectives and the **copula**. Every active word follows the same two rules.

items: **Only the last kana changes.** Everything before it is as fixed as a noun: the う-row kana of a verb, the い of an adjective, the だ of the copula.
**Every change is a stem with a helper.** The て-form and the past are not magic conjugations: a stem is made, then a helper (-て, -た, -ない, -ば, -そう ...) is attached.

blocks.text: You already know the first one (あ, い, う, え, お stems). The second is the **て-stem**, which is used for -て, -た and also -たら and -たり. The last kana decides the stem:
An adjective drops its い or turns it into か, け or く. Each stem takes its own helpers.

rows: ない, て, and alone as an adverb
高く, 高くない, 高くて

blocks.en: (I) run fast. (the く-stem as an adverb)

blocks.jp: 昨日の映画は面白かった。

blocks.en: If it is cheap, (I) will buy it.

blocks.jp: 弟はおもちゃを欲しがる。
blocks.en: My little brother shows signs of wanting a toy.

blocks.text: The copula だ is one kana, so it borrows a rider: だっ + た = だった, だろ + う = だろう, and its て-form is で. It is less regular because it has no relatives to be regular with.
今日は休みだった。 Today was a day off.

items: Nouns never change; they only take particles.
Verbs, adjectives and the copula change only their last kana, always by stem plus helper.

questions.instruction: Which is the て-form of 待つ?
questions.note: つ becomes っ, then て.

questions.instruction: Which is the て-form of 読む?
questions.note: む becomes ん, then で.

questions.instruction: Which is the て-form of 歩く?
questions.note: く becomes い, then て.

questions.instruction: Which is the て-form of 出す?
questions.note: す becomes し, then て.

questions.instruction: Which is the て-form of 遊ぶ?
questions.note: ぶ becomes ん, then で.

questions.instruction: Pick the past form of 暑い
questions.note: The かっ-stem plus た.

questions.instruction: Pick the ば-form of 寒い
questions.note: The けれ-stem plus ば.

questions.instruction: Which is the adverb form of 早い (early, fast)?
questions.note: The く-stem works as an adverb.

questions.instruction: Which says "looks delicious"?
questions.note: For そう, drop the い and attach the helper.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.note: The copula's past is だっ + た.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 彼は学生＿＿、まだ十八歳だ。
questions.note: The て-form of the copula is で.
questions.en: He is a student and is only eighteen.

questions.instruction: True or false?
questions.prompt: Nouns change their last kana like verbs.
questions.note: Static words such as nouns never change.

questions.instruction: True or false?
questions.prompt: 食べる → 食べて changes only the last kana.
questions.note: Only the last kana changes: る becomes て.
questions.en: 食べる becomes 食べて.

questions.instruction: Which is NOT a correct て-form?
questions.note: す becomes し, so 話して is correct.

questions.instruction: Which endings become ん and then で?
questions.note: ぬ, ぶ and む all give ん + で.

questions.instruction: How many stems does an adjective have?
questions.note: く, かっ, けれ and the dropped-い stem.

questions.instruction: What is the て-form of the copula?
questions.note: だ borrows で for its て-form.

questions.instruction: Tap the copula in the past
questions.note: だっ + た = だった.

questions.instruction: Tap the adjective in its て-stem
questions.note: The く-stem plus て: 安くて.
questions.en: The cakes at this shop are cheap and delicious.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: If it is hot, I open the window.
questions.note: The けれ-stem plus ば makes the condition.
questions.en: If it is hot, I open the window.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: My younger sister wants a new book.
questions.note: 欲しがる: the dropped-い stem plus がる.
questions.en: My younger sister wants a new book.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I bought bread and drank milk.
questions.note: て-stem 買って and past 飲んだ.
questions.en: I bought bread and drank milk.

questions.instruction: Which sentence is correct?
questions.note: ぐ becomes い, then だ.
